verses.text: Wisdom built herself a house and carved out seven pillars for it.
She got the meat ready, mixed her wine, and set the table.
She sent out her young servants, and from the highest spots in town she calls,
“If you don't know any better, come on in!” To anyone short on sense, she says,
“Come get some of my bread! Drink the wine I mixed!
Leave those naive ways behind and live. Walk the road where you'll learn to understand.”
Correct a mocker, and you'll get insulted. Call out a wicked person, and you'll get abuse.
Don't correct somebody who just wants to mock you. They'll hate you for it. Correct a wise person, and they'll love you for it.
Give wise people a lesson and they'll get wiser. Teach people who do right and they'll learn even more.
Wisdom starts with standing in awe of the LORD. Knowing the Holy One is what it means to understand.
With me, you'll get more days and add years to your life.
If you're wise, you're the one who benefits. If you mock, you're the one who'll carry the cost.
Folly is loud and out of control. She doesn't know a thing.
She sits in her doorway on a seat high up in the city.
She calls to people passing by who are just going straight down their own roads.
“If you don't know any better, come on in!” To anyone short on sense, she says,
“Stolen water tastes sweet. Food you eat on the sly hits different.”
What they don't realize is that the dead are in there. Her guests are already deep in the grave.
